newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chechen leader says Russian minister opposes peace.
newsitem.headline: Chechen leader says Russian minister opposes peace.

text.p: GROZNY, Russia, June 17 (Russia) - Chechen President Aslan Maskhadov accused Russian Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov on Tuesday of trying to derail the peace process between Moscow and the breakaway region.
"When everything's fine in Chechnya and everything's fine between Russia and Chechnya, then it's bad for Kulikov," Maskhadov told a news conference in the Chechen capital, Grozny.

The regional leader, whose peace deal last month with President Boris Yeltsin aims to prevent a return to war, praised the constructive approach of other Kremlin officials, including Security Council deputy secretary, Boris Berezovsky.

Berezovsky had criticised Kulikov at the weekend, saying he was "at a loss to understand" the interior minister's apparent attempts to prevent an exchange of Chechen prisoners for Russian interior ministry troops held captive in the region.
Kulikov is one of the few Kremlin hawks to survive Yeltsin's disastrous military attempt launched in 1994 to crush the Chechen separatist movement.
Chechen leaders have accused him in the past of being one of a shadowy "party of war" interested in prolonging the conflict.

Maskhadov said he was disappointed that a crackdown against hostage-taking gangs, Operation Shield of Law, launched on Monday, had failed to free a number of Russian journalists being held captive in Chechnya. Other hostages were released, however.

He claimed success for his drive to assert control over criminal elements and hardline groups unsatisfied with his treaty with Moscow. Several maverick armed units had already been demobilised, he said.
